description: Saskatoon will hold a by-election for School Division Ward 5.

School Division will cover all associated costs.
Modern Erratics Project installed three recycled material sculptures for $297,000.
Located at Material Recovery Center, Diefenbaker, and Forestry Farm Parks.
Council debated removing the public art funding policy.

chips.text: Saskatchewan arts and culture sector contributes over $1 billion to provincial GDP.
Councillor Donauer consistently opposed the 1% public art funding policy.
Local artists, fabricators, and contractors benefited from project investment.
Councillor Parker supported removing funding, citing resident concerns about sidewalk repairs.
Trade agreements prevent the city from requiring local procurement for art projects.
Waste reduction from recycled art contributes to avoiding $120M landfill cost.
Mayor Block signaled a motion to improve public art communication and funding avenues.

speakers.name: Tristan Surtees
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Public Art Policy and the Modern Erratics Project
said: Investment directly returns to the local Prairie economy.
Public art is an asset, not a one-time expense.
The project created an associate artist role for skills transfer.

speakers.name: Kelsey Ford
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Public Art Policy and Modern Erratics Project
said: Maintain the civic capital project funding stream.
Public art reflects community identity and provides social, economic benefits.
Improve city communication about public art's purpose and cost.

speakers.name: Daniel Macdonald
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: City's Public Art Policy
said: Opposes motion to eliminate capital arts funding project.
Politicians should educate themselves on art's value.
Arts and culture contribute significantly to GDP and jobs.

speakers.name: Jean-Sébastien Gauthier
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: City's Public Art Policy
said: Supports maintaining 1% for Arts Policy as proven investment.
Public art creates business opportunities for local fabricators.
The policy strengthens skills and a dynamic economy.

speakers.name: Stephanie Bellefleur
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: City's Public Art Policy
said: Has grave concerns about municipal systems supporting artists.
Advocates for championing and supporting artists in partnership with public.
City's website and communication with artists are challenging.

description: Proposes removing 1% public art funding from large city capital projects.

chips.text: Policy allocates up to 1% of capital projects over $5M, max $500,000.
Councillor Donauer was quoted saying, 'I'm not an art guy,' sparking debate.
Local artists, fabricators, designers, and other skilled workers are affected.
Several public delegations spoke against removing the public art funding stream.
Councillor Donauer believes 1% funding is too much and disconnects from public perception.
Trade agreements may prevent local procurement requirements for public art projects.
Policy supports reconciliation and marginalized communities, including BIPOC and LGBTQQ+.
Public art can enhance messages about environmental sustainability and recycling.
Administration committed to improving communication around future public art projects.

speakers.name: Bryn Rawlyk
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Councillor R. Donauer - City's Public Art Policy
said: Public art brings dynamic elements and people to the city.
1% of private construction money could fund arts.
City council has power to engage this funding lever.

speakers.name: Daniel Macdonald
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: City's Public Art Policy
said: Opposes the motion to eliminate capital arts funding.
Councillor Donauer's "not an art guy" stance is problematic.
Politicians should educate themselves about art, not attack it.

speakers.name: Ella Dawn McGeough
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Councillor R. Donauer - City's Public Art Policy
said: Supports maintaining the 1% public art policy.
Public art is integral to shaping and experiencing shared places.
Eliminating policy confuses criticism of outcome with principle.

speakers.name: Jean-Sébastien Gauthier
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: City's Public Art Policy
said: Supports maintaining the 1% policy as an investment in artists.
Public art creates business opportunities for local industry.
Policy builds civic identity and artistic legacy.

speakers.name: Stephanie Bellefleur
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: City's Public Art Policy
said: Has grave concerns about municipal systems supporting artists.
Dismantling the 1% system would be disheartening.
City website and communication with artists are challenging.

speakers.name: Andrew Keith
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Councillor R. Donauer - City's Public Art Policy
said: Art transcends time, producing culture, connection, human engagement.
City Hall should create an ecosystem for artists to thrive.
Zero funding is definitely not the answer for public art.
